reproduction_target: A predominantly wet-lab chromatin-accessibility study in Schizosaccharomyces pombe. The authors build a copper-inducible, auxin-degron-controlled DNA methyltransferase system (Dam and M.SssI expressed from the urg1 locus) to probe DNA accessibility in living cells, and compare it with methylation of isolated nuclei in vitro. The computational reproduction target is the analysis chain that converts the resulting sequence data into accessibility measurements: (1) Illumina paired-end sequencing of DpnI-digested, re-ligated genomic DNA followed by per-GATC methylated-fraction computation via the authors' previously published SnakemakeMethylFrac workflow; (2) Nanopore sequencing with Dorado basecalling using the sup v5.2.0 model plus the 5mCG_5hmCG modification model, Dorado alignment against both the PomBase reference and a strain-specific de novo assembly, methylated-read filtering, and 5mCpG calling with modkit; (3) canu de novo assembly of the SPT999a strain genome from Nanopore reads, with rDNA, dg/dh pericentromeric-repeat (MUMmer) and mating-type-locus (Liftoff) annotation; (4) re-analysis of published H3K9me2/3 ChIP-seq data (GEO GSE280066) through fastp, Bowtie2, SAMtools and MACS to annotate heterochromatin domains; (5) a previously published decaying-sine-wave model applied to average nucleosome-phasing data; and (6) retrieval of protein and RNA vegetative-growth expression levels from PomBase.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS source XML (fetched with curl and a browser User-Agent; WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on the JATS URL). The Methods contain one short 'Computational analysis' subsection plus computational sentences embedded in the 'Nanopore sequencing' subsection; both were mined. The declared code artifact is a FigShare anonymous private-share link (https://figshare.com/s/69f60ea30371853387b9), which is not a code repository landing page in the GitHub/GitLab sense: it has no DOI, no version, no file listing reachable without JavaScript, and no README prose. Therefore NO README prose was available to read at Stage 1, and every code-axis score below rests on Methods prose only. Nine wet-lab procedures (plasmid construction, strain construction, induction time courses, G1 arrest, genomic DNA extraction, Illumina library preparation, nuclei isolation and in vitro Dam methylation, Nanopore library preparation, immunoblotting) are recorded as layer W / OOS and are excluded from S.
capture_claim_note: The paper pins exact versions for most named third-party tools (Dorado v1.0.0 with basecalling model dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_sup v5.2.0 and modification model 5mCG_5hmCG v1; modkit v0.5.0; canu/2.2; MUMMER/4.0.1; liftoff v1.6.3; fastp/0.24.0; Bowtie2 v2.5.3; SAMtools v1.21; macs v3.0.0) but claims no environment closure of any kind: no lockfile, no container image or digest, no conda/pip specification, no language runtime version, and no release tag or commit for the authors' own SnakemakeMethylFrac workflow or decaying-sine-wave model. The FigShare deposit is an anonymous private-share URL, not a versioned release snapshot with a DOI, so 'release_snapshot' was considered and rejected. Under protocol v0.2.6 exact_pins_partial is NOT on the positive Stage-2 gate (Delta-2 caps version at 1 from the prose read, so a code check yields no R-star gain), hence stage2_candidate=false; this paper can only reach Stage 2 through the orchestrator's stratified audit draw.

steps.label: Nanopore basecalling with Dorado v1.0.0 - verbatim: 'Reads were basecalled using Dorado v1.0.0 with the dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_sup v5.2.0 basecalling model and 5mCG_5hmCG v1 modification model (--min-qscore 8)'. Tool, both model identities and the quality threshold are all pinned; input reads are the study's own Nanopore data, deposited under GEO GSE313347 which is private until 2026-12-23

Alignment of basecalled Nanopore reads with the Dorado aligner - verbatim: 'Reads were aligned to both the Pombase reference genome and our de novo assembly for SPT999a (see below) using the Dorado aligner'. No aligner options are given, no PomBase genome release/build identifier is given, and which downstream figure uses which of the two references is not stated

Methylated-read filtering - verbatim: 'We filtered reads with at least one 5mCG site (mCG threshold > 0.9 and unmethylated CG < 0.1)'. Both numeric thresholds are given, but no tool, script name or implementation is named for this filtering step

5mCpG site calling with modkit v0.5.0 - verbatim: 'The 5mCpG sites from filtered bam files were called using modkit v0.5.0 (--cpg --combine-strands --ignore h)'. Version and full option string are pinned

Per-GATC methylated-fraction computation, the central quantitative readout of the paper - verbatim: 'Methylated fractions for GATC sites were calculated using the SnakemakeMethylFrac workflow 17'. Reference 17 is a prior Nature Communications paper by the same group (Prajapati et al. 2025), not a repository URL. No workflow version, tag, commit, container or parameter set is given here, and no Snakemake version is named

Nucleosome-phasing analysis with the authors' decaying-sine-wave model - verbatim: 'Our decaying sine wave model was used to analyze average phasing data 45'. Reference 45 is a prior Science Advances paper (Xu et al. 2025). No implementation, version, fitting procedure, initial values, or fitted-parameter table is given in this paper

De novo assembly of the SPT999a chromosome sequences with canu/2.2 - verbatim: 'with parameters: genomeSize=13m, maxInputCoverage=300, rawErrorRate=0.03, correctedErrorRate=0.01, corOutCoverage=100, minReadLength=10000'. Version and a complete parameter list are given; the input Nanopore reads are under the embargoed GSE313347

Manual/literature-based annotation of the mitochondrial sequence and the rDNA locus - verbatim: 'We included the mitochondria sequence from the Pombase reference genome. The rDNA locus in the reference genome was annotated based on the Pol I initiation site 50 and the BoxI terminator 51'. No tool, no coordinates, no procedure and no PomBase release are given

Annotation of pericentromeric dg and dh repeat elements with MUMMER/4.0.1 - verbatim: 'The dg and dh elements are annotated by the dg and dh elements in the left pericentromeric region of chromosome I using MUMMER/4.0.1 52'. Version pinned, but no MUMmer subcommand (nucmer/promer), no alignment options, and no identity/length thresholds for calling an element are given

Mating-type locus annotation with Liftoff - verbatim: 'The mating locus was annotated using liftoi v1.6.3 53' (OCR/typography artefact for 'liftoff'; reference 53 is Shumate & Salzberg, Liftoff). Version pinned, but the source annotation GFF and its PomBase release are not identified and no Liftoff options are given

Pre-processing of published H3K9me2/3 ChIP-seq reads with fastp/0.24.0 - verbatim: 'we used ChIP-seq data from GSE280066 54, which were pre-processed by fastp/0.24.0 55'. Input accession is public (GSE280066, HTTP 200) and the version is pinned, but no fastp options (adapter sequences, quality/length cutoffs, deduplication) are stated and the specific GSM samples/replicates used are not enumerated

ChIP-seq alignment to the SPT999a de novo genome with Bowtie2 v2.5.3 - verbatim: '(-X 5000 --very-sensitive --no-discordant --no-mixed --no-unal) 56'. Version and full option string given; input data public (GSE280066); the index is built on the paper's own assembly, which is itself only obtainable via the embargoed read set or by request
Alignment filtering with SAMtools v1.21 - verbatim: 'Aligned reads were filtered using SAMtools v1.21 (-f 0x2 -F 0x300 -q 1) 57'. Version and full flag set given

H3K9me2/3 peak calling with macs v3.0.0 and replicate merging - verbatim: 'H3K9me2 and H3K9me3 peaks were predicted using macs v3.0.0 58; the peaks from their three replicates were combined to annotate H3K9me2/3 regions'. Version pinned, but no MACS subcommand, no effective genome size, no q-value or fold-enrichment cutoff, no broad/narrow choice, no input/control assignment, and no definition of how the three replicates were 'combined' (union? intersection? IDR?)

Retrieval of protein and RNA expression levels - verbatim: 'Protein and RNA expression levels were obtained from Pombase 59 using data for vegetative growth 22, 23'. PomBase is a public resource, but no release/build identifier, no download date, no file name and no query or filtering procedure is given

Plasmid construction (p856, p964, p951, p998 and intermediates p850, p960, p990, p846) by synthetic-fragment insertion and restriction cloning - verbatim: 'All plasmids and their verified sequences are available upon request.' No sequence deposit, no Addgene entry for the new plasmids (only the pre-existing Addgene 169353 backbone is cited)
S. pombe strain construction (SP1L, SP3L, SP12L, SP15L, SP27L) by transformation and drug selection; strains listed in Supplementary Table 1; integration confirmed by PCR
Induction time courses for Dam (SP3L, 0.4 mM CuSO4) and M.SssI (SP15L, 1 mM CuSO4) with 100 nM aIAA degron control, sampling at 0/30/60/120/240 min
G1 arrest by nitrogen starvation (EMM no-nitrogen, 8 h at 25 C), microscopic verification of arrest, then Dam induction time course
Genomic DNA extraction by SDS/TE washing, lyticase digestion, chloroform extraction, isopropanol precipitation, RNase A treatment and AMPure XP purification
Illumina paired-end library preparation: DpnI digestion, AMPure purification, HiFi Taq DNA ligase re-ligation, library preparation 'as described 16', sequencing on an Illumina NextSeq-2000

Nuclei isolation from 972h- cells (spheroplasting, Ficoll step gradient) and in vitro Dam methylation at 0/1.5/2.9/5.6/10.0 nM Dam for 30 min at 25 C - the in vitro comparator for the in vivo accessibility measurement
Nanopore library preparation and sequencing: PureLink genomic DNA purification, NEBNext ONT companion end-repair module, ONT Native Barcoding kit SQK-NBD114.24, ONT MinION flow cell
Immunoblotting for HA-tagged Dam/M.SssI with anti-HA 3F10 (1:2500) and anti-tubulin ab-185067 (1:10000) loading control, Azure 600 imaging

headline.static_readiness: 0/15 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI on 5/15 computational steps (C1 Dorado basecalling, C4 modkit, C7 canu assembly, C12 Bowtie2, C13 SAMtools), NI on 6/15 (C2 Dorado aligner, C3 methylated-read filtering, C9 MUMmer, C10 Liftoff, C11 fastp, C14 MACS), X on 4/15 (C5 SnakemakeMethylFrac, C6 decaying-sine-wave model, C8 rDNA/mitochondrial annotation, C15 PomBase retrieval). The binding constraints are two, and they act on different sets of steps. First, the parameter axis: six tools are named and version-pinned but invoked with no options at all (Dorado aligner, MUMmer, Liftoff, fastp, MACS, plus the unspecified PomBase query), so those steps cannot rise above NI on prose. Second, the two analyses that produce the paper's headline quantities - the per-GATC methylated fraction (SnakemakeMethylFrac) and the nucleosome-phasing fit (decaying sine wave) - are the authors' own code, cited only as prior publications with no version, no URL, no parameters, which pushes exactly the most load-bearing steps to X. The version axis is capped at 1 throughout because no environment closure is claimed anywhere. Note also that the primary sequence data (GEO GSE313347) is embargoed until 2026-12-23, so 11/15 steps carry a data axis of 1 rather than 2; the four steps at data=2 are those consuming the already-public ChIP-seq accession GSE280066 or PomBase.
headline.coverage: 15 computational steps and 9 wet-lab steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods prose. This is a mixed paper whose principal contribution is wet-lab (a copper-inducible, degron-controlled Dam/M.SssI accessibility assay in living S. pombe); the computational layer is a conventional Nanopore/Illumina/ChIP-seq analysis chain plus two in-house analysis modules inherited from the group's earlier papers. No README prose was available: the sole code artifact is an anonymous FigShare private-share URL that renders only via JavaScript and exposes no file listing, DOI or version to an unauthenticated fetch.

gaps.where: Data availability statement; inputs to C1-C7
gaps.missing: The primary sequence data are not yet accessible. Verbatim: 'The Illumina and Nanopore sequence data generated in this study have been deposited in the GEO database with accession code GSE313347.' A live check of that accession returned: 'Accession GSE313347 is currently private and is scheduled to be released on Dec 23, 2026.' No reviewer token is published in the preprint, so at Stage 1 the entire in vivo and in vitro methylation data set is inaccessible and every step that consumes it is capped at data=1.
gaps.how_to_close: Release GSE313347 (or publish the reviewer token alongside the preprint), and state which GSM samples correspond to which figure panel and time point.

gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'The code used to analyse the data is available at FigShare: https://figshare.com/s/69f60ea30371853387b9.' This is an anonymous private-share URL, not a citable deposit: it carries no DOI, no version number, no license, no file manifest reachable without JavaScript (the fetch returned HTTP 202 with an empty body to an unauthenticated agent), and figshare private-share links are revocable and not archived. The statement also does not say what the deposit contains - in particular whether SnakemakeMethylFrac (C5) and the decaying-sine-wave model (C6) are included, or only figure-plotting scripts.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the analysis code in a public version-controlled repository, mint a DOI-bearing archival snapshot (Zenodo/Software Heritage), add a license and a README that maps scripts to figures, and replace the private-share URL with the DOI.

gaps.where: C5 (SnakemakeMethylFrac), C6 (decaying sine wave model), C3 (read filtering)
gaps.missing: The three in-house analysis components carry no version identity at all. SnakemakeMethylFrac is referenced only through citation 17 (Prajapati et al., Nat Commun 16, 4577, 2025) with no repository URL, tag, commit or Snakemake version; the decaying-sine-wave model is referenced only through citation 45 (Xu et al., Sci Adv 11, eadw7108, 2025); the 5mCG read-filtering step names no implementation whatsoever. These are precisely the steps that generate the paper's headline accessibility and phasing numbers.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite SnakemakeMethylFrac by repository URL plus a specific tag or commit hash and record the Snakemake version used; do the same for the phasing-model code, and name the tool used for read filtering.

gaps.where: C2, C8, C10, C15 - all reference-genome and annotation resources
gaps.missing: No release identifier is given for any external biological resource. 'the Pombase reference genome' (C2, C8) has no assembly build or PomBase release; the Liftoff source annotation (C10) is not named; the PomBase protein and RNA vegetative-growth expression data (C15) have no release, download date or file name. PomBase is a continuously updated resource, so an unpinned reference silently changes the result over time.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the PomBase release version and download date for the genome FASTA, the annotation GFF and the expression tables, and deposit the exact files (or their checksums) alongside the code.

gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind is claimed: no container image or digest, no conda-lock/pixi/renv lockfile, no requirements or environment.yml, no language runtime version (Python/R), and no compute-platform description. Version pinning stops at the level of individual tool version strings, which is exact_pins_partial, not a lock.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock or container digest covering the full Dorado/modkit/canu/MUMmer/Liftoff/fastp/Bowtie2/SAMtools/MACS stack and the Snakemake workflow, and declare the platform it was resolved for.

gaps.where: C2 (Dorado aligner), C9 (MUMmer), C10 (Liftoff), C11 (fastp), C14 (MACS), C15 (PomBase query)
gaps.missing: Six steps name a version-pinned tool but give no invocation parameters at all. Specifically: Dorado aligner options and which of the two reference genomes was used for which analysis; the MUMmer subcommand and the identity/length thresholds used to call dg/dh elements; the Liftoff options and source annotation; the fastp adapter/quality/length settings and the list of GSM samples drawn from GSE280066; the MACS subcommand, effective genome size, q-value or fold cutoff, broad-vs-narrow choice and input/control pairing, plus the rule by which 'the peaks from their three replicates were combined' (union, intersection or IDR is not stated); and the PomBase query/filter used to obtain expression levels.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full command lines (or the Snakemake config) for every step, and state the replicate-combination rule for the H3K9me2/3 peak set explicitly.

gaps.where: C2, C12 and Results - dual reference genomes
gaps.missing: Reads are said to be aligned 'to both the Pombase reference genome and our de novo assembly for SPT999a', and the ChIP-seq is aligned to the SPT999a assembly, but the paper never states which reference underlies which reported figure, coordinate system or accessibility value. Because the pericentromeric dg/dh repeats - the central biological subject of the paper - are exactly where the two references are expected to differ, the ambiguity is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
gaps.how_to_close: State per figure which assembly was used, and deposit the SPT999a de novo assembly FASTA with a version so that coordinates are resolvable.

gaps.where: Methods - Plasmids and Strain construction (W1, W2)
gaps.missing: Physical reagents are gated behind personal request: 'All plasmids and their verified sequences are available upon request.' Neither the plasmid sequences nor the new strains are deposited in Addgene, the NBRP/YGRC S. pombe stock centre or any sequence archive, so the wet-lab layer is not independently re-derivable either. Recorded for completeness; wet-lab steps are OOS and do not affect S.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit plasmid sequences in GenBank and the plasmids/strains in Addgene and a fission-yeast stock centre, and cite the deposit identifiers.
